title: Switzerland Extension
description: Swiss succession rules: Pflichtteil (forced heirship, 2023 Erbrechtsrevision), cantonal inheritance tax variation, matrimonial property regimes, Erbschein (certificate of inheritance), and notarial will forms.
$comment: Swiss succession law recognises only three parenteles (ZGB Art. 457-466): 1. Descendants. 2. Parents and their issue (siblings, nephews/nieces). 3. Grandparents and their issue (uncles/aunts, cousins). There is no fourth parentele — unlike Germany which extends to unlimited Ordnungen. If no heir is found in the three parenteles, the estate goes to the canton.
dataProvenance: Swiss Civil Code (ZGB) Art. 457–640, January 2023 succession law reform (Erbrechtsrevision)

pflichtteil.description: Pflichtteil — the statutory reserved portion under Swiss law. Since the 2023 Erbrechtsrevision (ZGB Art. 470–480), parents are no longer protected heirs; descendants retain 1/2 of their intestate share and the surviving spouse 1/2 of their intestate share.

reformApplies.description: Whether the January 2023 Erbrechtsrevision rules apply (deaths on or after 1 January 2023)

protectedHeirs.description: Array of persons entitled to a Pflichtteil under Swiss law

personId.description: Reference to the Person.id of the protected heir

heirClass.description: Class of protected heir. Since 2023, only descendants and surviving_spouse are protected heirs; parent is included for pre-2023 deaths.
heirClass.$comment: parent is no longer a protected heir since the 1 January 2023 reform (revision of the Swiss Civil Code, in force 1 January 2023). The enum value is retained for pre-2023 estates. The 2023 reform increased the freely disposable share from 3/8 to 1/2 (when there are descendants and a surviving spouse).

statutoryShareFraction.description: The heir's intestate statutory share as a fraction, e.g. 1/2

pflichtteilFraction.description: The Pflichtteil as a fraction of the estate (half the statutory share since 2023), e.g. 1/4

availableQuota.description: The freely disposable quota remaining after all Pflichtteile are reserved

fraction.description: Available quota as a fraction of the net estate, e.g. 1/2

estimatedValue.description: Estimated monetary value of the available quota in minor currency units

cantonalVariation.description: Cantonal inheritance tax and succession law variation. Switzerland has 26 cantons; direct-line heirs are exempt in most cantons, but rates and exemptions differ significantly.

canton.description: Two-letter canton abbreviation (e.g. ZH, BE, GE, VD, BS)

cantonalTaxApplies.description: Whether cantonal inheritance tax applies to this estate

cantonalTaxRate.description: Cantonal inheritance tax rate as a percentage

linealHeirsExempt.description: Whether lineal heirs (descendants and surviving spouse) are exempt from cantonal inheritance tax in this canton

matrimonialPropertyRegime.description: The matrimonial property regime governing the split of matrimonial property before succession begins. participation_in_acquisitions is the default regime under ZGB Art. 181.

erbschein.description: Erbschein — the Swiss certificate of inheritance (Erbenbescheinigung) issued by the competent cantonal authority confirming the identity of heirs and their shares.

issued.description: Whether an Erbschein has been issued

issuingAuthority.description: Name of the cantonal authority that issued the Erbschein

issueDate.description: Date on which the Erbschein was issued

referenceNumber.description: Reference or case number of the Erbschein

notarialWillForm.description: Form of will used under Swiss law. public_will: notarially authenticated before two witnesses (ZGB Art. 499–508). holographic_will: entirely handwritten, dated, and signed by the testator (ZGB Art. 505). oral_will: emergency oral will before two witnesses when notarial form is impossible (ZGB Art. 506–508).
